prompts.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Create one revised 3D INTERIOR CONCEPT of the TRAVELING FROG'S OWN HOME, portrait 4:5. The user wants the familiar original decoration back and a MODERATE cozy scale, after rejecting a cavernous nearly empty stone hall.
INPUT ROLES: Reference1, tiny original-game interior screenshot, is the PRIMARY layout and furniture language: tree trunk on left, mushroom steps spiraling up left, blue bedding upstairs, jars and rounded stove under loft, little round stump table on green leaf rug. Reference2, larger illustrated furnished room, is supporting decor language: rounded organic furniture, broad leaves as fabric/curtains, green moss-shaped textiles, compact lived-in nooks, enclosed grey rock shell. Reference3, actual 3D frog, fixes frog identity and matte character style. Do not import the previous generic stone tea hall's layout.

Compose a close but readable three-quarter whole-room view from just INSIDE the front of the closed stone house, seeing the loft and ground floor together, gently elevated storybook perspective, NOT wide-angle, not a dollhouse floating in a forest. Stone back and side walls and curved ceiling enclose all sightlines. No exterior grass, sky or outside forest through missing walls.
RESTORE THESE DISTINCTIVE ANCHORS: one warm natural tree trunk on LEFT side, slimmed so it doesn't dominate or hide the room (roughly 0.6 frog-heights wide); pale shelf-mushroom spiral treads around it, visibly continuous from ground to loft. Timber mezzanine across BACK half, blue futon/single bed and muted rose small woven mat above, little pinned postcards/books, simple low twig railing with open stair landing. Under loft at back-right are open wooden shelves with clay jars, hanging herbs and one rounded cream TWO-HOLE cooking stove. Ground CENTER contains a low ROUND TREE-STUMP table with visible end grain, one candle and small tea cup, two little stump stools; underneath is a broad soft GREEN LEAF/MOSS-SHAPED RUG. A leaf cloak on a simple stand near front/left and small travel chest near side wall. One draped large leaf curtain at upper left, simple circular wood window in rear rock wall, compact warmth and useful little objects rather than empty gallery floor.
SCALE CORRECTION: one sleepy green frog, matching reference3 exactly, with cream belly, dark half-lidded eyes, slim arms and two recognizable hind feet, stands visibly at the round table. The frog is an identifiable main inhabitant, not a tiny speck. Target room width10-11 frog-heights, depth8.5-9.5, loft deck height3.0, roof about6.2; table diameter1.6F, table height0.55F; bed length2.2F. Keep a modest route around table and clear stair foot, approximately30% free usable floor, NOT a vast empty foreground. Frog visually about14-17% of image height in this whole-room composition. Furniture fits frog; bed and stove not giant. Do not make the frog a huge mascot either.
Materials: warm light grey CONTINUOUS NATURAL STONE enclosing walls with gentle irregular planes and only sparse cracks; no masonry brick courses, no bark walls. Ground pale warm stone with muted green leaf/moss textiles rather than a huge blue-grey paving plaza. Honey wood, sage/olive leaf greens, muted cyan-blue bedding, soft pink rug; broad simple sculpted forms, delicate hand-painted softness, matte surfaces, NOT gritty photorealistic rough cave, not glossy toys. Soft warm daylight, readable gentle shadows, no blown highlights or neon greens.
No Chinese palace decoration, no generic straight wall stair replacing the mushroom steps, no rectangular tea table. Exactly one frog, no other animals, no text, UI, watermarks or logos. Faithful to the original frog home's cozy organic furnishing vocabulary, now translated into appealing three-dimensional game art.

Use case: stylized-concept. Create one alternative HOME FOR THE PANDA, with a restrained Chinese-inspired bamboo-and-tea interior, portrait4:5.
INPUT ROLES: Reference1 is the previous generated stone-home image, now reassigned to the PANDA'S house; retain its rock volume, rear loft, right wall staircase, round windows, warm sunlight and tea-space spirit, but make room moderately more compact. Reference2 is a 3-view sheet of ONE panda, the character identity reference. Reference3 is a supplied illustrated decorated room, supporting round lattice-window, bamboo furniture, paper/leaf textile and intimate two-floor furnishing language.
One panda only, no green frog and no other animals. Make the same round cream-and-charcoal panda with sleepy eyes and muted sage neckerchief clearly visible seated by the low tea table, a small tan tea satchel beside it. Animal is a resident comfortably using its own furniture, not a tiny dot in a grand hall. The panda body takes roughly14-17% of image height. Room feels10-11 resident heights across with less empty floor than reference1.
Keep the familiar stone envelope and rear loft: upstairs a modest BAMBOO low bed with muted ochre linen quilt on the LEFT, small bamboo writing desk and cushion RIGHT; small brown wooden stair climbing RIGHT wall. Ground floor: low rounded rectangular bamboo-and-wood tea table, two plain woven straw cushions, compact tea cabinet and small ceramic kettle. Make Chinese influence visible but understated: round moon-window with restrained geometric Chinese lattice, a narrow ink-wash mountain scroll without any writing, pale bamboo folding screen near left wall, one small warm paper lantern, one slender potted bamboo. A celadon tea pot and two cups on the table. No red-and-gold abundance, palace roofs, dragon ornaments, giant Chinese characters or busy cultural decorations.
Continuous warm grey/ivory natural rock walls, gently irregular slate floor softened by a simple small woven mat, warm light wood and bamboo, celadon green, linen ochre. Stylized smooth sculpted game-art quality to match frog and panda, warm and softly hand-crafted rather than gritty realism. Camera inside the enclosed house, no missing walls/outside panorama, moderate three-quarter perspective with floor and loft visible. A little closer/cozier than reference1, plenty of detail but not furniture overload. No text, labels, logos, watermark or UI. This is clearly a different resident's home, with a quiet Chinese tea-room sensibility.
